sections.heading: II. FSM Arithmetic
sections.intro: Design FSMs that compute the following functions.

callouts.body: **Don't** design an SC first to get your solution; **do** think through the FSM directly.

Function composition **does not work** for FSMs. You can't combine two +1 machines to get a +2 machine.

This has to do with the fact that FSM diagrams show states of the *overall* machine, not the flow of information *through* it.

sections.heading: III. FSM Navigation
sections.intro: For each of the following navigation tasks, design an FSM which solves it.

callouts.body:
Use the following abbreviations:

Inputs:
0 = **E** (Empty)
1 = **B** (Block)

Outputs:
11 = **F** (Forward)
00 = **S** (Stop)
10 = **R** (Right)
01 = **L** (Left)

questions.label: Problem 1
questions.title: State abstraction
questions.statement: Construct a state table for the following machine, then convert it to a FSM diagram. What function does it compute in binary?

figures.alt: Two half-adder (HA) stages in series: the input feeds the first HA; each HA’s carry C loops back through a NOT gate, an M block and a NOT gate into that HA’s upper input; the first HA’s sum S feeds the second HA; the second HA’s sum S is the output

questions.label: Problem 2
questions.title: Multiple realizability
questions.statement: Consider the following two SCs. What function does each compute in binary? Do they implement the same FSM? Why or why not? Show your work.

figures.alt: A: the input splits into both inputs of a first half-adder; its sum S feeds a second half-adder; the two carries C join at an OR gate, then pass through a NOT gate, an M block and a NOT gate into the second half-adder’s upper input; the second half-adder’s sum S is the output. B: the input passes through a NOT gate, an M block and a NOT gate to the output

questions.label: Problem 14
questions.title: Way Finder
questions.statement:
Given *any* non-branching maze, make your way all the way through, and keep going.

A **non-branching maze** is a path that never branches and is never wider than 1-cell across, except on corners where two 1-cell width paths may intersect. Here is an example.*
